title: The CSV challenge: ten legal CSV files against hand-rolled parsers and Scout's picks

input.why: A header and two rows. Everything should pass this.
A field that contains a comma is wrapped in quotes. Customers named "Smith, Jane" exist.
A quote inside a quoted field is written twice.
A quoted field may contain a line break. Addresses do this all the time.
input.csv:
name,address
Ada,"1 Main St
Springfield"
Lin,2 Side St

input.why: The standard line ending is CRLF. Windows and Excel write it.
The last record may or may not end with a line break.
Missing values are empty strings, not missing columns.
Files often end with an extra blank line. It is not a customer.
Excel's "CSV UTF-8" export starts with an invisible byte order mark. It is not part of the first header.
Spaces are part of a field and must not be trimmed away.
